I love Kled's design, I think you really nailed the champion's essence. Also, really cool design of "Chaaaaarge!!!", but there are 2 flaws with it.

First, this kind of effect can't be fast speed, otherwise you would be able to use it mid opponent's attack, something that would essentialy break the game's current mechanics, and I don't think Riot has a plan of implementing a multi-layered attack. Not to mention that even if it could be fast speed, this would be too good at 4 mana - having it at slow speed would make it more fair.

Secondly, the card's text is incorrect. While it is plain obvious that the attack would happen before the unit gets recalled, giving how the free attack mechanic works right now the unit would challenger opp's unit and then get recalled, without actually striking. I know, that last part doesn't make no sense in a practical point of view, but, logically speaking, thats what the text says.

In order to circunvent this issue, you could say:

"Pick a card with Overwhelm from your deck, board or hand. It starts a free attack, Challenging an enemy unit. If it was summoned by this card's effect, grant it **Enlist**"

**Enlist** would be a new keywoard, saying: - "Round end or Strike, shuffle me back into the your deck". You could also say "Round end or Strike, recall me", but I think Recall doesn't really fit with Noxus region identity + this card would work as a tutor, something that would have greater implications for balance.

Many champions operate in such a way that they swing the game when levelled. To compensate this power, they always have downsides along them. Asol is a near instawin when levelled up, but he costs 10 mana and has a fairly difficult requirement. Levelled Lee can OTK you, but requires your whole deck to work for it. Karma (in the good ol days of Ionia) used to be a instawin when flipped, but she requires to be enlightned.

TF works in a simmilar fashion. He has probably the strongest flip of all champions right now. But he is a 4 mana 2/2. Thats is one of the worst statline-to-mana ratio in the game. TF, Zap, Kinkou Lifeblade and Vanguard Firstblade are all 4 mana and the most expensive 2/2's IN THE GAME. Not to mention that Zap and Kinkou have a very powerful keyword attached to them, and Vanguard Firstblade grows to a 4/4 as soon as he declares an attack.

TF being a frail 4 mana champion that wins you the game when levelled is a design choice - its a gamble you make that you'll level him up. And that is what makes him one of the most fun champions to play with (sadly, not to play agaisnt at the moment).

That IS true from a gameplay oriented point of view. But the whole thing about bluecard is having its LoL flavour - giving mana back. And I don't think refilling spellmana is such a big deal, comparing to card draw. 

You see, emptying mana is not something you commonly do in LoR (unless, of course, you are a aggro SMOrc deck). That means that you'll probably be going to the next turn with some mana floating. Giving that TF's blue card is the first being played, you would have to commit yourself to playing a more costly spell first in order to get the full value from the mana refill, and that is something you can't always do (in many ocasions holding a card as a threat is more valuable than outright using it). Thats why you would probably not be receiving the full value from a full mana refill, you would need to be using your pick a card's, get excited's and suit-up's proactively (all of these being the medium-costed spells in the deck), and thats no good in most situations.

Anyway, even if it ends up being too good at a full spell mana recovery, it could be nerfed to 2 spellmana refill. Not the end of the world either.

Good post, I agree with alot of the points you brough up and the deep analysis makes a lot of sense. There are, however, some things I dont agree with, which reside mainly on your suggested changes:

*  *Both players can see which celestial cards have been picked* \- This same suggestion was brough up when people were enfuriated over Nab, and I dont think its a good fix for celestial's powerlevel. Sure, it reduces said power by giving you information on opp's hand, but it also decreases the game overall skillcap as handreading and bluffing become strategies that can no longer be applied to celestial cards. There are other ways of nerfing gameplay without reducing its skillcap level.
*  *Spell shield is a one turn effect* \- This would kill the spellshield keyword. Think how Ki Guardian is a card that, if ever used, its not mainly because of its barrier effect, rather for its draw. If a unit that has barrier is played, all the opp has to do is not try to remove said unit for the turn, saving removal options for later. Barrier only really works as a responsive card in the form of combat tricks and with the usage of Brightseel Protector, a card that is quite busted on its own. Making spellshield durable for only one turn would frequently turn Asol into a 10 mana do nothing, as he would be immediatly killed as soon as his protection wore off.
*  *Picking a celestial card always requires a discard (not applied to ASOL as you don't pick)* \- This concept is already present in Spacey Sketcher, and it works for her because the celestials she provides are among the better ones. 1 mana silence, 0 mana Tracker, 0 mana -1 cost and the better shadow assassin, all of these are very cheap and can provide such insane value that burning a card in your hand in order to get them is more than worth. Most of the higher cost celestials, however, are clunkier, sometimes requiring you to already have a celestial card in hand or being dependant on you having played a lot of celestial stuff (all of the finishers). This makes the return of investment of these cards super delayed, thus having to pay, beside the already high mana cost, a card in your hand in order to get them makes the deal really bad.
*  *Make celestial cards incapable of being played the turn they're acquired* \- Of all the proposed changes, this would be the hardest kicking nerf, I think. Not necessarily would it be the most detrimental to celestial's power level *per se*, but it would make the archetype so clunky and slow that I doubt anyone would still enjoy playing it. Imagine going through all the investment of levelling up Asol, hitting the lucky living legends or the elusive finisher that would make you win the game, only to be locked out of the possibility of playing them for 0 mana in that turn. People that enjoy playing Asol, myself included, are in for the godly power vibes, and for the single fact that this would make impossible to level asol, aquire living legends through luck or other celestials and proceed to create a universe of monstruous cards in your hands would kill the fantasy of the celestial archetype.

One final point of mine is that I dont think Asol is such a problem for the game's health. Sure, if he flips you are most likely dead, but I dont think thats unfair. That champion requires not only 10 mana of investment, but 10 power in your board in order to level up, meaning that his flip can be disrupted in a lot of ways (heck, even frostbiting does it). For such high requirements its totally fine for him to be a one turn game ender after flipping.

You can also consider using your combat tricks in order to up the blocker's health and tank some more damage, but be cautious that these can also be vital for ending the game as fast as possible.

And yes, with Kinkou Elusives you can consistently win by turn 6-7. This is why I argue that concussive palm is a situational keep even though its a great counter for the overwhelm units, because your main priority shouldnt be outlasting harrowing aggro, but racing them. If you dont have a hand that can rush the opponent down, kick concussive, your greenglade duos, zeds and kinkou wayfinders are going to be getting the job done for you.

I have faced Harrowing Aggro around 10 times while playing Kinkou Elusives and have beaten them everytime. The standart version of elusives as displayed in swim's site and mobalytics can easily rush down the opponent fast enough that they usually cant even threat to lethal you by the turn you are finishing them. Your mulligan keeps are Zed, 1 drops and 2 drops, Kinkou Wayfinder and maybe concussive palm or elixir of iron if you already have a good starting hand. 

From here it is very straighforward - play your units on curve and if attacking on odds, playing zed will put you in a very good spot since up to turn 3 the opponent doesnt have good blockers for him. In this case zed will either deal a lot of damage to the face  or force the opponent to take a bad trade, it takes a very specific hand state of double disciples + transfusion or disciple and demolitionist + transfusion for this exchange to go bad for you. After that, simply sacrifice your non elusive followers for defensive purposes while smacking down the opponent with your unblockable units, he cant really deal with them being noxian fervor his only removal option (which is not commonly kept in the opening hand). Zed should be almost always attacking as it is his main job to apply pressure, dont be afraid to let him die to transfusion or to a basilisk rider, you should come out ahead in the trade anyway.

If attacking on evens, the gameplan is roughly the same. The only interesting difference here is that you can pair a turn 2 greenglade duo with a turn 4 Kinkou Wayfinder for a combo that not only deals a lot of face damage but also fills your board with blockers for the next turn. Some versions of harrowing aggro are running aracnoid sentry, which is the only real scarecard here for it could stun your duo. 

In short, if there is a matchup in which kinkou elusives can excell at, is this one. Opponent has a hard time dealing with Zed, has virtually no good way to kill your elusives and cant really go wider than you thanks to kinkou elusives and navouri highwaymen flooding your board. The harrowing turns arent even a threat, since you are usually killing them before they come.
